title: "Larrea Growth Enviromental Analysis"
Author: Mariii Huff 
Date: March 14, 2026
output: github_document

###############################################################################
# OVERVIEW
This project analyzes a dataset examining variation in growth environment among
populations of Larrea species. The dataset was obtained from the repository 
maintained by the Environmental Data Initiative and includes observations 
collected between 2006 and 2009 from multiple geographic locations across North 
and South America. The study focuses on two species, Larrea tridentata and Larrea
divaricata, which are desert shrubs commonly found in arid environments. 
Data were collected from several sites including the Sevilleta National 
Wildlife Refuge in New Mexico, locations in Mexico, and sites in Argentina. 
The dataset includes variables such as species, site location, latitude, and 
growth environment, which allow researchers to examine how environmental 
conditions differ across plant populations.

The goal of this project is to investigate how growth environment varies among 
Larrea populations across species and geographic locations. Specifically, this 
project will explore whether patterns in growth environment differ between
species or across different sites. I hypothesize that growth environment will 
vary among locations because plants growing in different regions experience 
different environmental conditions such as temperature, soil composition, 
and water availability. Understanding these patterns may help explain how 
environmental factors influence plant populations and contribute to processes 
such as Local Adaptation.
###############################################################################

###############################################################################
# WORKFLOW
First, the dataset will be imported into R from the downloaded CSV file.
Next, the structure of the dataset will be examined to identify the variables 
and check for missing values. The data will then be cleaned by filtering out 
rows with missing values in key variables such as species, latitude, and growth 
environment. After cleaning the data, summary statistics will be calculated to
understand the distribution of observations across species and growth
environments. Several visualizations will then be created, including bar graphs 
and scatterplots, to explore patterns between species, geographic location, and
growth environment. Finally, the patterns observed in the graphs will be 
interpreted to determine whether growth environments vary among Larrea 
populations across different locations.
###############################################################################

############################################################
# SECTION 1: LOAD REQUIRED PACKAGES
############################################################

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

############################################################
# SECTION 2: IMPORT DATA
############################################################
To find an appropriate dataset, I queried the Environmental Data Initiative
website. Local Adaptation to Freezing in High and Low Latitude Populations 
of L. tridentata is the title of the dataset. Here is the link to the website: https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?packageid=knb-lter-sev.227.275475

RUN THIS CODE. Make sure to save this to your working directory. 
larrea <- read_csv("sev277_larreafreeze_20140107.csv")

############################################################
# SECTION 3: INSPECT DATA STRUCTURE
############################################################
Let's explore this dataset structure. Run these codes. 

head(larrea)

str(larrea)

summary(larrea)

names(larrea)

dim(larrea)

############################################################
# SECTION 4: CHECK FOR MISSING VALUES
############################################################
Most of the time we have missing values in the dataset. Let's run this code to 
see. 

colSums(is.na(larrea))

############################################################
# SECTION 5: CLEAN / TIDY DATA
############################################################
Time to make our dataset clean and neat for people to read. Run this code. 

clean_data <- larrea %>%
  filter(!is.na(species)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(latitude)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(growth_environment))

############################################################
# SECTION 6: VERIFY CLEAN DATA
############################################################
To make sure we did the clean up process right; run these codes. 

head(clean_data)

nrow(clean_data)

summary(clean_data)

############################################################
# SECTION 7: UNIQUE VALUES
############################################################
Let's explore the unique values of data that is in the two columns - Species &
Growth Environment. Run this code.

unique(clean_data$species)

unique(clean_data$growth_environment)

############################################################
# SECTION 8: SUMMARY STATISTICS
############################################################
 RUN THIS CODE FOR SPECIES SUMMARY. 
 
species_counts <- clean_data %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(count = n())

species_counts

RUN THIS CODE FOR GROWTH ENVIRONMENT SUMMARY. 

environment_counts <- clean_data %>%
  group_by(growth_environment) %>%
  summarise(count = n())

environment_counts

############################################################
# SECTION 9: LATITUDE STATISTICS
############################################################
Let's get the summary for the latitude on this dataset. Run this code.  

latitude_summary <- clean_data %>%
  summarise(
    mean_latitude = mean(latitude),
    min_latitude = min(latitude),
    max_latitude = max(latitude),
    sd_latitude = sd(latitude)
  )

latitude_summary

############################################################
# SECTION 10: SPECIES BY ENVIRONMENT
############################################################
Let's run this code for cleaning up the species & growth environment. 

species_environment <- clean_data %>%
  group_by(species, growth_environment) %>%
  summarise(count = n())

species_environment

############################################################
# SECTION 11: BAR GRAPH – GROWTH ENVIRONMENT
############################################################

Let's make a bar graph. RUN THIS CODE. 

ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = growth_environment)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Growth Environments",
    x = "Growth Environment",
    y = "Count"
  )

############################################################
# SECTION 12: BAR GRAPH – SPECIES COUNTS
############################################################
 Let's make another bar grapht. RUN THIS CODE.

ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = species)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Observations per Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Count"
  )

############################################################
# SECTION 13: SPECIES VS ENVIRONMENT
############################################################

Let's make a scaterplot. RUN THIS CODE. 

ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = species, fill = growth_environment)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Species Distribution Across Growth Environments",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Count"
  )

############################################################
# SECTION 14: LATITUDE HISTOGRAM
############################################################

Let's make a histogram. RUN THIS CODE. 

ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = latitude)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20) +
  labs(
    title = "Latitude Distribution",
    x = "Latitude",
    y = "Count"
  )

############################################################
# SECTION 15: LATITUDE BY ENVIRONMENT
############################################################

Let's add some things to our graph. RUN THIS CODE. 

ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = latitude, fill = growth_environment)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20) +
  labs(
    title = "Latitude Distribution by Growth Environment",
    x = "Latitude",
    y = "Count"
  )

############################################################
# SECTION 16: LATITUDE VS SPECIES
############################################################
Let's make a graph showing the latitude vs. species. RUN THIS CODE.

ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = latitude, fill = species)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20) +
  labs(
    title = "Latitude Distribution by Species",
    x = "Latitude",
    y = "Count"
  )

############################################################
# SECTION 17: BOX PLOT LATITUDE BY SPECIES
############################################################
Let's make a box plot by the latitude by species. RUN THIS CODE.

ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = species, y = latitude)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Latitude Range by Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Latitude"
  )

############################################################
# SECTION 18: BOX PLOT LATITUDE BY ENVIRONMENT
############################################################
Let's make another box plot but this time for latitude by environment.
RUN THIS CODE.

ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = growth_environment, y = latitude)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Latitude Range by Growth Environment",
    x = "Growth Environment",
    y = "Latitude"
  )

############################################################
# SECTION 19: SORT DATA
############################################################
Let's run this code to sort our data. 

sorted_data <- clean_data %>%
  arrange(latitude)

head(sorted_data)

############################################################
# SECTION 20: CREATE SUBSETS
############################################################
Let's create subsets for our dataset. Run these codes. 

species_tridentata <- clean_data %>%
  filter(species == "Larrea tridentata")

species_divaricata <- clean_data %>%
  filter(species == "Larrea divaricata")

############################################################
# SECTION 21: PLOT SUBSET DATA
############################################################
Now we can plot this subsets of dtata. Run these codes.

ggplot(species_tridentata, aes(x = latitude)) +
  geom_histogram()

ggplot(species_divaricata, aes(x = latitude)) +
  geom_histogram()

############################################################
# SECTION 22: EXPORT CLEAN DATA
############################################################
Let's export our date and then finally clea up anything that looks untidy.
RUN THIS CODE. 

write_csv(clean_data, "clean_larrea_data.csv")

############################################################
# SECTION 23: SAVE SUMMARY TABLES
############################################################
Let's save our tables to our working directory. Run these codes. 

write_csv(species_counts, "species_counts.csv")

write_csv(environment_counts, "environment_counts.csv")

############################################################
# SECTION 24: FINAL CHECKS
############################################################
Run this code and we are done. 

print("Analysis Complete")
